Read on drafting, and read again on review.** The `paper-authoring`\n4\tskill and the `prose-reviewer` agent both consume this file, so a rule cannot mean one\n5\tthing while writing and another while reviewing.\n6\t\n7\t⚠️ **This is the shared FLOOR, not the whole review.** The reviewer additionally carries\n8\treader-outcome questions that do not appear here and that an author must never be given as\n9\ta checklist: a generator optimises against any list it can see. See the skill's §\"Why the\n10\treviewer knows things this file does not\".\n11\t\n12\tEvery rule below was derived from a measured sweep of the 21-bundle corpus, not from a\n13\tstyle guide. Where a number appears, it is what was counted.\n14\t\n15\t---\n16\t\n17\t## 1. The em-dash: prohibited outright, including in headings\n18\t\n19\t**Never write `---` or a literal `—`.** Two forms exist and both are banned.\n20\t\n21\t**Why this one is absolute.** An em-dash reads as machine-authored to a 2026 reader and\n22\tcosts trust before the physics is evaluated. One is as disqualifying as forty, so there is\n23\tno acceptable density. Enforced by `validate.py --check bundle_prose_em_dash_free`, target\n24\tzero. Measured before the corpus was swept: **741 of them, and 0 of 21 bundles clean.**\n25\t\n26\t### ⚠️ The en-dash `--` is MANDATORY and must never be touched\n27\t\n28\t`--` (exactly two hyphens) is a different character doing a different job, and the corpus\n29\tcarries **1,121** of them:\n30\t\n31\t- compound eponyms: `Bose--Einstein`, `Bekenstein--Hawking`, `Schwinger--Keldysh`,\n32\t  `Kaul--Majumdar`, `Chowdhury--Hartnoll--Hebbar--Khondaker`, `SK--EFT`\n33\t- numeric ranges: `pp. 10--15`, `$2$--$3$ K`\n34\t\n35\t**An author over-correcting to \"no dashes at all\" breaks every compound name in the\n36\tprogram, and the check cannot see it** because it counts exactly three hyphens. This is the\n37\tsingle highest-cost mistake available here. One live line contained both:\n38\t`observables---also drives the SK--EFT`.\n39\t\n40\tA third variant exists in the wild: the literal Unicode en-dash `–` (U+2013), found as\n41\t`Kaul–Majumdar` and `Chowdhury–Hartnoll–Hebbar–Khondaker`. Write `--` instead; D3 once\n42\tspelled the same name both ways.\n43\t\n44\t### Replacing an em-dash is a REWRITE, not a substitution\n45\t\n46\tA mechanical swap produces comma splices. Identify the job the dash was doing, then use the\n47\tpunctuation that already exists for that job. Frequencies below are from six independent\n48\treadings of all 741 occurrences.\n49\t\n50\t| The dash was doing | Frequency | Write instead |\n51\t|---|---|---|\n52\t| Paired aside interrupting a clause | ~45–55% | parentheses; a comma pair when the aside is short and contains no commas of its own |\n53\t| Introducing an explanation, expansion or list | ~30–45% | a colon |\n54\t| Separating a label from its gloss in `\\item`, `\\subsection{}`, `\\paragraph{}` | ~15% | a colon, always |\n55\t| Contrastive \"X, not Y\" interjection | ~7% | a comma pair (parentheses would demote a correction to an aside) |\n56\t| Joining two independent clauses | ~3–15% | a semicolon, or a full stop and a new sentence |\n57\t| Trailing appositive glossing a number's significance | common in E1/E2 | a comma |\n58\t\n59\t### The four hard cases, each of which defeats a mechanical fix\n60\t\n61\t1. **The aside contains its own parenthetical or citation.** Converting the outer dash to\n62\t   parentheses yields stacked or nested parens that read as a stutter:\n63\t   `(\\lean{diamondDist_eq_choiSDP}) (the Watrous semidefinite program~\\cite{Watrous2018}) is proven`.\n64\t   **Merge the tag and the aside into ONE parenthetical** with an internal comma or\n65\t   semicolon. Do not nest.\n66\t2. **The aside contains a comma-separated list.** Comma-punctuating it makes the reader\n67\t   parse the inner items as continuing the outer sentence's list. Use parentheses.\n68\t3. **The sentence already has a colon later on.** Adding a second colon reads as a nested\n69\t   label. Restructure with a copula: `X is the headline theorem: Y`.\n70\t4. **Three levels of subordination.** An aside inside an aside inside a main clause is a\n71\t   sentence trying to be three sentences. Split it.\n72\t\n73\t### The generative habits behind them: prohibit these, not just the symbol\n74\t\n75\tAll six readers converged on the same root, so treat it as the rule that matters:\n76\t\n77\t> **Do not interrupt a main clause to insert a clarification.** Write the clarification as\n78\t> its own sentence, before or after.\n79\t\n80\tThe dominant shape was *claim, dash, restatement-with-a-twist, dash, continuation*: draft a\n81\tclean declarative, then, worried a reader will misattribute a convention or miss a caveat,\n82\tsplice the qualifier into the middle. It concentrated in exactly the paragraphs doing the\n83\theaviest epistemic hedging (novelty disclaimers, provenance caveats, convention-pinning),\n84\twhich is where this project's prose is densest.\n85\t\n86\tFour more shapes, each of which reliably produces an em-dash:\n87\t\n88\t- **Name-then-gloss in itemised lists.** `\\item \\verb|foo_bar|: the substantive witness`.\n89\t  Use the colon from the start; this was the single most common pattern in the Lean-heavy\n90\t  bundles.\n91\t- **Label-then-gloss in headings.** `\\subsection{Pillar 1: Golterman--Shamir}`. A dash in a\n92\t  heading also reads as a tic when scanning the table of contents.\n93\t- **Tag-stacking.** A claim ending in a `\\lean{...}` identifier in parens, then a dash\n94\t  glossing that identifier. This is an appositive that got dash-punctuated only because the\n95\t  sentence had already spent its parentheses.\n96\t- **Claim-then-immediately-re-scope.** `T_H \\approx 2.4$ K --- nine orders of magnitude\n97\t  above atomic BEC --- with adiabaticity...`. A defensible instinct for a rigorous program,\n98\t  executed with the wrong punctuation: pick the syntax that matches the qualifier's\n99\t  grammatical role.\n100\t\n101\t---\n102\t\n103\t## 2. A fix may not narrate itself\n104\t\n105\t**Never tell the reader what an earlier draft of this paper said, when it was corrected, or\n106\twhich review round caught it.** A referee has no access to that process and cannot act on\n107\tit; the text reads as a changelog pasted into a manuscript.\n108\t\n109\tEnforced by `validate.py --check bundle_reader_facing_voice`, target zero. Banned forms:\n110\t\n111\t- a correction stamped with a date: `(corrected 2026-08-01)`\n112\t- an account of an earlier draft: `three earlier drafts of this paragraph asserted...`\n113\t- a first-person superseded claim: `We previously shipped a theorem asserting...`\n114\t- an internal review reference: `(D11 Stage-13 round-14 finding 6.2)`\n115\t- the project's own planning documents: `Our earlier planning documents described...`\n116\t- review rounds cast as actors: `rounds 7 and 10 both rated this cosmetic`\n117\t- a claim about the paper's own drafting: `typeset unconditionally in every draft`\n118\t\n119\t**The history is not lost, it moves.** `papers/<X>/change_log.md` and\n120\t`docs/review_finding_supersessions.json` are where a later reader can actually check it, and\n121\tthe ledger entry is required by the lift procedure anyway.\n122\t\n123\t### ⚠️ Removing narration is not deleting content\n124\t\n125\tMost of these passages wrap something real, and the substance must survive:\n126\t\n127\t- **A retraction is a scientific disclosure.** Restate it as a present-tense negative\n128\t  result: what is *not* claimed and why it fails. Do not delete the paragraph.\n129\t- **A scope correction states the correct scope.** Keep every factual statement about what\n130\t  a module does and does not contain, including file:line references. Drop only \"earlier\n131\t  drafts called it X\" and the date/round/finding tag.\n132\t- **A completeness disclaimer is a real caveat.** Keep it; drop the account of what two\n133\t  earlier drafts asserted.\n134\t\n135\t### What is NOT prohibited\n136\t\n137\tReporting that *the literature* corrected something is ordinary scholarship: `Smith\n138\tcorrected this coefficient in 2019` is correct and stays.\n139\t\n140\tDescribing the verification pipeline is legitimate **when the pipeline is the paper's\n141\tsubject matter** (I1, and I2/I3 for library conventions). Addressing the paper's own\n142\treferees is legitimate anywhere: `lets Mathlib4 reviewers calibrate expectations`.\n143\t\n144\tThis distinction is why the rule targets the *act* of self-narration rather than a\n145\tvocabulary. A word list banning `Stage 13`, `reviewer` and `adversarial review` scores 90\n146\thits on this corpus, of which 48 are legitimate uses in the methodology paper alone.\n147\t\n148\t---\n149\t\n150\t## 3. Claim discipline\n151\t\n152\tThese are enforced elsewhere in the pipeline; they are repeated here because they are\n153\tcheaper to satisfy while drafting than to repair at review.\n154\t\n155\t- **Never hedge a count or numerical literal with \"alt convention\" or \"+N depending on\n156\t  convention\" without proving the convention sensitivity.** If counts disagree across\n157\t  tools, find the truth. Convention-drift framing masks actual content drift: a \"161 ± 3\n158\t  alt convention\" was really 164, and the +3 was real drift.\n159\t- **Verify which registry a name lives in before citing it.** `AXIOM_METADATA`,\n160\t  `PLACEHOLDER_THEOREMS`, `HYPOTHESIS_REGISTRY` and `BORDISM_HYPOTHESES` are four different\n161\t  tables; a name found in one and attributed to another is a Stage-13 blocker.\n162\t- **Every cross-language prior-art claim must resolve to a verifiable URL or canonical\n163\t  ecosystem reference.** Hallucinated libraries have shipped before. When in doubt, cite\n164\t  the ecosystem (UniMath, Mathlib4) rather than naming a specific library.\n165\t- **When broadening an attribution, verify every addition belongs in the broadened\n166\t  category.** Surface code is abelian-stabiliser QEC, not non-Abelian-anyon TQC.\n167\t- **Numbers come from the pipeline.** Use `\\input{tables/<spec>.tex}` and the `counts.tex`\n168\t  macros rather than typing a literal.\n169\t\n170\t---\n171\t\n172\t## 4. Structure\n173\t\n174\t- **The abstract leads with the result**, not with the programme, the architecture, or what\n175\t  the paper will do.\n176\t- **The reader never sees the project's internal taxonomy.** Not `bundle`, `tier`, `wave`,\n177\t  `phase`, or `splash`. Companion papers are cited as papers, by title, in a normal\n178\t  reference list. This is what makes a manuscript read as a repository index: F's organising\n179\t  vocabulary was its own publication plan.\n180\t- **Section architecture is authored, not accumulated.** A bundle's sections come from its\n181\t  charter, written before any source is registered. Do not add a section because a source\n182\t  was registered: D3 has 37 sections against 31 sources, which is sedimentation.\n183\t- **Every figure is planned.** A bundle with no figures is a charter defect, not a style\n184\t  choice; 9 of 21 bundles shipped zero figures because the lift step only ever *migrated*\n185\t  figures that already existed.\n186\t"}]},"uuid":"4ba8179f-b04a-4301-bce5-989d94ffc97a","timestamp":"2026-08-15T19:37:24.587Z","sourceToolAssistantUUID":"8c4ae549-37bb-415d-80f2-c35e9a3396d9","userType":"external","entrypoint":"claude-desktop","cwd":"/Users/johnroehm/Programming/PythonEnvironments/Physics/Fluid-Based-Physics-Research/SK_EFT_Hawking","sessionId":"6cf37aa2-f1c7-4e33-a712-f17c2d75d99b","version":"2.1.229","gitBranch":"HEAD","slug":"swift-singing-llama"}

{"parentUuid":"4a345a96-2bab-4f3c-9c61-ef7ba77056b5","isSidechain":true,"promptId":"d7b89794-41f0-46fe-9a20-6d198f8f624f","agentId":"a78a58dec52c8d1d6","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01FMqkDKKyKg3xqHhZZwctAk","type":"tool_result","content":"1\t---\n2\tname: paper-authoring\n3\tdescription: This skill should be used when the user asks to \"draft a paper section\", \"write the bundle draft\", \"author the manuscript\", \"lift content into a bundle\", \"write up this wave for publication\", \"draft the abstract\", \"revise the paper prose\", or when editing any `papers/<bundle>/paper_draft.tex`. Provides the house voice, the prohibited-pattern floor, and venue conventions for SK-EFT Hawking publication bundles.\n4\t---\n5\t\n6\t# Authoring a publication bundle\n7\t\n8\tGuidance for writing manuscript prose in `papers/<bundle>/paper_draft.tex`. This is the\n9\tgenerative counterpart to the `prose-reviewer` agent; both read the same prohibited-pattern\n10\treference so a rule cannot drift between writing and review.\n11\t\n12\tRead it either way you draft: the lead writing in-context, or a `paper-drafter` agent\n13\tdispatched over one section. `paper-drafter` reads this file and the same reference by\n14\tpath, so the floor is identical however the prose is produced.\n15\t\n16\t**Read `references/prohibited-patterns.md` before drafting.** It is mandatory, not\n17\tbackground, and it is short.\n18\t\n19\t---\n20\t\n21\t## Why this skill exists\n22\t\n23\tThe pipeline had three reviewer agents and no authoring guidance. Everything about how to\n24\twrite lived in `docs/BUNDLE_LIFT_PROCEDURE.md` §7 as a bookkeeping checklist consulted at\n25\tlift time. The measured result of that gap, across 21 bundles:\n26\t\n27\t- **741 em-dashes**, with zero bundles clean\n28\t- **13 passages** narrating the paper's own correction history to a referee\n29\t- **9 of 21 bundles shipping zero figures**, because the lift step only migrated figures\n30\t  that already existed and no step ever planned one\n31\t- **D3 carrying 37 sections against 31 contributing sources**, which is sedimentation\n32\t  rather than architecture\n33\t\n34\tNone of that is a capability limit. It is what an unguided generator produces when the only\n35\tcontrols are downstream reviewers.\n36\t\n37\t---\n38\t\n39\t## Before writing a section\n40\t\n41\t1. **Read the charter.** `papers/<X>/bundle_metadata.json` carries `target_journal` and\n42\t   `length_target`; the section belongs to a planned outline, not to a source paper that\n43\t   happened to be registered.\n44\t2. **Read the substrate directly.** Contributing per-paper drafts, the Lean modules, the\n45\t   roadmap. Do not write from a summary.\n46\t3. **Know the claim this section makes** and which apex theorem backs it. A section whose\n47\t   claim has no Lean witness is a finding waiting to happen.\n48\t\n49\t## While writing\n50\t\n51\tWrite for a referee at the named venue who has never seen the repository, cannot run the\n52\tcode, and will not read a second sentence to understand the first.\n53\t\n54\t- **State the result, then support it.** Not the programme, not the architecture, not what\n55\t  the section will do.\n56\t- **One clause, one job.** Do not interrupt a main clause to insert a clarification; write\n57\t  the clarification as its own sentence. This single habit produced most of the corpus's\n58\t  em-dashes.\n59\t- **No em-dash, ever** (`---` or `—`). **`--` is mandatory** for compound eponyms and\n60\t  ranges and must never be touched. Both rules and every replacement case are in\n61\t  `references/prohibited-patterns.md` §1; read them before reaching for a dash.\n62\t- **A fix never narrates itself.** Correct silently in the manuscript and record the history\n63\t  in `change_log.md` and the supersession ledger (§2 of the reference).\n64\t- **Numbers come from the pipeline** via `\\input{tables/<spec>.tex}` and the `counts.tex`\n65\t  macros, never typed as literals.\n66\t- **Cite companion work as papers**, by title. The reader never sees `bundle`, `tier`,\n67\t  `wave`, `phase` or `splash`.\n68\t\n69\t## Before handing off\n70\t\n71\t```bash\n72\tuv run python scripts/compile_bundle_pdf.py <X>   # must be clean\n73\tuv run python scripts/validate.py \\\n74\t    --check bundle_prose_em_dash_free \\\n75\t    --check bundle_reader_facing_voice \\\n76\t    --check bundle_manuscript_length\n77\t```\n78\t\n79\tCompile through `compile_bundle_pdf.py`, never `pdflatex` inside `papers/<X>/`. An in-place\n80\tcompile clobbers `paper_draft.{aux,log,synctex.gz}`, and a reviewer running concurrently then\n81\tjudges your draft by a `.log` that belongs to someone else's pass.\n82\t\n83\tAll three are deterministic and all three must pass. They are a floor, not a review: they\n84\tconfirm nothing prohibited is present, and say nothing about whether the argument carries.\n85\t\n86\t---\n87\t\n88\t## Why the reviewer knows things this file does not\n89\t\n90\tThe `prose-reviewer` agent reads this same reference, so the two never disagree about a\n91\trule. It also carries a brief that is deliberately **not** written down here, framed on\n92\treader outcome rather than rule compliance: where a reader would stop, whether the abstract\n93\tleads with the result, whether each section advances a single argument.\n94\t\n95\tThat asymmetry is intentional. A generator optimises against any checklist it can see, so a\n96\treviewer briefed entirely off the author's rules would pass anything the author produced.\n97\tSatisfying this file is necessary and not sufficient.\n98\t\n99\t---\n100\t\n101\t## Additional resources\n102\t\n103\t### Reference files\n104\t\n105\t- **`references/prohibited-patterns.md`** — mandatory read. The em-dash prohibition and its\n106\t  replacement cases, the self-narration ban, claim discipline, structure rules. Shared with\n107\t  the `prose-reviewer` agent.\n108\t\n109\t### Related surfaces\n110\t\n111\t- `docs/BUNDLE_LIFT_PROCEDURE.md` — the 14-step lift workflow this drafting sits inside\n112\t  (§7 authoring, §11 the BLOCKER loop, §12a the terminal de-scarring pass).\n113\t- `docs/WAVE_EXECUTION_PIPELINE.md` Stage 10 — the process law and its gates.\n114\t- `docs/BUNDLE_DIRECTORY_SCHEMA.md` — `length_target`, `apex_theorems`, and who writes what.\n115\t"}]},"uuid":"710177bb-ea27-4b5a-a403-34616e664abe","timestamp":"2026-08-15T19:37:34.569Z","sourceToolAssistantUUID":"4a345a96-2bab-4f3c-9c61-ef7ba77056b5","userType":"external","entrypoint":"claude-desktop","cwd":"/Users/johnroehm/Programming/PythonEnvironments/Physics/Fluid-Based-Physics-Research/SK_EFT_Hawking","sessionId":"6cf37aa2-f1c7-4e33-a712-f17c2d75d99b","version":"2.1.229","gitBranch":"HEAD","slug":"swift-singing-llama"}
{"parentUuid":"557d77ed-f818-4a27-9bfe-2d2041796a62","isSidechain":true,"promptId":"d7b89794-41f0-46fe-9a20-6d198f8f624f","agentId":"a78a58dec52c8d1d6","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_015G2awWqymY1WP39Fw9S2WC","type":"tool_result","content":"740\tquantitatively negligible at GW170817 frequencies but is the empirical\n741\ttarget of the vestigial-metric Monte Carlo of \\S\\ref{sec:vestigial-mc}.\n742\t\n743\t\n744\t%% =====================================================================\n745\t%% §7 — Bekenstein–Hawking entropy from MTC state counting\n746\t%% Lift: paper26_bh_entropy\n747\t%% =====================================================================\n748\t\n749\t\\figuredeferred{fig:d3-gw170817-constraint}{the natural-$\\chi$ range against the GW170817 cap; L1 carries this figure as \\texttt{fig\\_c\\_GW\\_vs\\_ligo\\_constraint} and the deep version must not duplicate the splash one, so its framing waits on the L1/D3 split being settled}\n750\t\\section{Bekenstein--Hawking entropy from MTC state counting}\n751\t\\label{sec:bh-entropy}\n752\t\n753\tThe substrate's microscopic entropy account ships a Kaul--Majumdar\n754\tSU(2)$_k$ logarithmic correction with an explicitly negative\n755\tcoefficient~\\cite{KaulMajumdar2000}, and an abelian-MTC falsifier that\n756\tserves as a structural no-go on alternative microscopic theories.\n757\t\n758\t\\subsection{Closed form and Kaul--Majumdar coefficient}\n759\t\n760\tFor a Schwarzschild horizon of area $A$ in Planck units of the emergent\n761\t$G_N$,\n762\t\\begin{equation}\n763\t\\label{eq:bh-entropy}\n764\tS(A) \\;=\\; \\frac{A}{4G_N}\n765\t- \\frac{3}{2}\\log\\!\\bigl(A/(4G_N)\\bigr) + O(1)\\,,\n766\t\\end{equation}\n767\t\\noindent\n768\twhere the $-3/2$ logarithmic coefficient\n769\t(\\texttt{BHEntropyMicroscopic.kaul\\_majumdar\\_log\\_coefficient}) reads\n770\toff the SU(2)$_k$ Chern--Simons partition function on the horizon. The\n771\tprefactor matches the Verlinde formula at large area\n772\t(\\texttt{verlinde\\_matches\\_kaul\\_majumdar\\_at\\_large\\_area}) and decomposes as\n773\t$-3/2 = -1/2$ (Gaussian saddle) $-1$ (logarithmic Verlinde-formula\n774\tmodular-transform piece)\n775\t(\\texttt{kaul\\_majumdar\\_log\\_decomposition}). The $1/4$ in $A/(4G_N)$ is, in the\n776\tLQG/Verlinde-counting route of this section, a horizon boundary-condition (Immirzi)\n777\ttuning; in the ADW Sakharov induced-gravity route it is derived Immirzi-independently\n778\t(\\texttt{InducedGravityEntropy.frolov\\_fursaev\\_quarter\\_coefficient}, Wave~9): the\n779\tsame Seeley--DeWitt $a_2$ that induces $G_N$ also fixes the horizon entanglement-entropy\n780\tarea density, with the heat-kernel-to-Einstein--Hilbert ratio structurally $4$ (FFZ,\n781\thep-th/9607104). The $-3/2$ log is genuinely derived from the literal SU(2) singlet count:\n782\t\\texttt{verlindeEntropy\\_SU2k} is now (Wave~7C) the \\emph{faithful} $\\Gamma$-Catalan\n783\tlog-dimension $\\log\\!\\bigl[\\Gamma(2x{+}1)/(\\Gamma(x{+}1)\\Gamma(x{+}2))\\bigr]$ at\n784\t$x = A/(8 G_N \\log 2)$, a genuine analytic object, not the earlier saddle self-definition\n785\t(closing substrate-audit \\#13), and the Kaul--Majumdar closed form is a \\emph{derived\n786\tcorollary}: \\texttt{gaussianSaddleAsymptotic} is the genuine $O(1/A)$ rate\n787\t$\\bigl|\\texttt{verlindeEntropy\\_SU2k}(A,G_N) - \\texttt{kaulMajumdarS}(A,G_N,\\kappa_{\\mathrm{KM}})\\bigr|\n788\t= O(1/A)$ with the literal constant $\\kappa_{\\mathrm{KM}} = \\tfrac{3}{2}\\log(2\\log 2) -\n789\t\\tfrac{1}{2}\\log\\pi$. The discrete singlet count carries the sharp $O(1/m)$ rate\n790\t(\\texttt{LaplaceMethodAsymptotic.log\\_singletCount\\_sub\\_rate}); the continuum $O(1/A)$ rate\n791\trests on a \\texttt{Real.Gamma} Stirling-with-remainder built kernel-pure from Mathlib primitives\n792\tvia a Bohr--Mollerup convexity squeeze\n793\t(\\texttt{GammaStirling.logGamma\\_sub\\_stirlingPart\\_isBigO}, previously absent from Mathlib),\n794\twith no Hardy--Ramanujan input. The two routes are consistent\n795\t(\\texttt{frolov\\_fursaev\\_matches\\_kaulMajumdar\\_leading}).\n796\t\n797\t\\subsection{Five falsifier theorems for the boundary-condition bundle}\n798\t\n799\tThe horizon-MTC boundary-condition tracked-hypothesis bundle carries\n800\tfive falsifier theorems\n801\t(\\texttt{H\\_HorizonBoundaryCondition\\_falsifier\\_positivity},\n802\t\\texttt{\\_falsifier\\_logBound},\n803\t\\texttt{\\_falsifier\\_secondLaw},\n804\t\\texttt{\\_falsifier\\_quarterCoefficient},\n805\tand an envelope\n806\t\\texttt{H\\_HorizonBoundaryCondition\\_implies\\_nonabelian\\_envelope}). Each\n807\tfalsifier is a constructive obstruction.\n808\t\n809\t\\subsection{Witt-invariant sharpening of the anomaly-matching condition}\n810\t\n811\tThe bundle's anomaly-matching consistency field is sharpened beyond its perturbative form\n812\t(Wave~8B). The horizon chiral central charge $c_- = 8 N_f$ satisfies the elementary mod-8\n813\tcondition $8 \\mid c_-$ for \\emph{every} $N_f$\n814\t(\\texttt{HorizonWittBoundary.horizon\\_wave8\\_anomalyMatch\\_always}), so on its own it does not\n815\tconstrain the ADW model. The genuine, non-vacuous consistency condition is Witt-triviality of the\n816\tboundary, $24 \\mid c_-$, which holds \\emph{if and only if $3 \\mid N_f$}\n817\t(\\texttt{horizon\\_wittTrivial\\_iff\\_three\\_generations}; unconditional, wiring the SymTFT\n818\tWitt-class machinery). The perturbative $8 \\mid c_-$ is exactly its necessary shadow\n819\t(\\texttt{wittTrivial\\_implies\\_mod8}), and the gap is strict: $N_f = 1$ passes $8 \\mid c_-$ but\n820\tfails $24 \\mid c_-$ (\\texttt{horizon\\_anomalyMatch\\_strictly\\_weaker\\_than\\_witt}). This ties the\n821\thorizon boundary condition to the program's three-generation result through the \\emph{same} Witt\n822\tinvariant. The physical reading, that Witt-triviality is equivalent to the boundary admitting a gapped\n823\t(Lagrangian-algebra) topological boundary, is the Davydov--M\\\"uger--Nikshych--Ostrik (2010, arXiv:1009.2117)\n824\tcorrespondence, of which the perturbative $8 \\mid c_-$ is only the necessary part.\n825\t\n826\t\\subsection{Abelian-MTC falsifier}\n827\t\n828\t\\texttt{abelian\\_MTC\\_falsifies\\_H\\_HorizonBoundaryCondition}: an abelian\n829\thorizon MTC cannot reproduce the Kaul--Majumdar $-3/2$ logarithmic\n830\tcoefficient on the same area. The\n869\t\\emph{regime-partition criterion} fixes which branch a given black hole\n870\tsits on by mass.\n871\t\n872\t\\subsection{Regime-partition mass $M_c$}\n873\t\n874\t\\begin{equation}\n875\t\\label{eq:Mc-regime}\n876\tM_c \\;=\\; \\frac{N_f\\,\\Lambda_{\\mathrm{UV}}}{12\\pi\\,\\alpha_{\\mathrm{ADW}}}\\,.\n877\t\\end{equation}\n878\t\\noindent\n879\t\\texttt{BHThermodynamicsFourLaws.M\\_c\\_pos} certifies $M_c > 0$;\n880\t\\texttt{regime\\_partition\\_criterion} states the biconditional that a\n881\tblack hole sits on the Schwarzschild branch if and only if its mass\n882\texceeds $M_c$, and on the ADW-extremality branch otherwise.\n883\t\\texttt{classify\\_Schwarzschild\\_iff} and\n884\t\\texttt{classify\\_ADWExtremality\\_iff} discharge the two\n885\tmutually-exclusive directions; \\texttt{classify\\_Boundary\\_iff} closes the\n886\tboundary case $M = M_c$. At the natural microscopic point\n887\t$(\\Lambda_{\\mathrm{UV}},N_f,\\alpha_{\\mathrm{ADW}}) = (M_{\\mathrm{Pl}},16,1)$,\n888\t$M_c \\approx M_{\\mathrm{Pl}}/(12\\pi/16) \\approx M_{\\mathrm{Pl}}/2.36$;\n889\tastrophysical black holes ($M\\gtrsim M_\\odot$) are unambiguously in the\n890\tSchwarzschild branch.\n891\t\n892\t\\subsection{Hawking-temperature profiles per regime}\n893\t\n894\tIn the Schwarzschild branch,\n895\t$T_H = 1/(8\\pi G_N^{\\mathrm{emerg}} M)$ is strictly decreasing in\n896\t$M$~\\cite{Hawking1975}\n897\t(\\texttt{T\\_H\\_schwarzschild\\_strict\\_decreasing}); in the ADW-extremality\n898\tbranch the cooling sign is anchored to the sonic-hole backreaction of\n899\tBalbinot \\textit{et al.}~\\cite{Balbinot2005}, whose emission temperature\n900\tdecreases as the hole radiates, against the Jacobson--Koike thin-film\n901\tcontrast~\\cite{JacobsonKoike2002}, whose\n902\t$T_H(v) = T_H(0)\\,(1 - v^2/c_\\perp^2)$ rises to a non-vanishing end\n903\ttemperature as radiation slows the wall; the substrate carries an\n904\texplicit cooling evolution\n905\t$T_H(t) = T_{H0}\\,e^{-t/\\tau_{\\mathrm{cool}}}$\n906\t(\\texttt{T\\_H\\_acoustic\\_evolution\\_strict\\_decreasing}). Formalizes the Bekenstein-Hawking entropy\n17\t`S = A/(4 G_N) − (3/2) log(A/(4 G_N)) + c_0` for a horizon S²\n18\tcarrying simple-object labels of a Modular Tensor Category (MTC),\n19\tfollowing Kaul–Majumdar (PRL 84, 5255 (2000), arXiv:gr-qc/0002040).\n20\t\n21\t**Scoping mode (per deep-research return).** This module ships in\n22\t**Outcome-3 (tracked-hypothesis) mode** for the general MTC case, with\n23\tan **Outcome-2 (Conditional) sub-corollary** specialized to SU(2)_k\n24\tunder the Kaul–Majumdar derivation. Phys. 321, 2 (2006), arXiv:cond-mat/0506438.\n70\t- McGough & Verlinde, JHEP 11, 208 (2013), arXiv:1308.2342 — closest published precedent.\n71\t- Phase 6a Wave 3 deep-research return.\n72\t- LinearizedEFE.lean (Phase 6a Wave 1) — `G_N_emerg` Sakharov closed form.\n73\t\n74\t-/\n75\t\n76\tnamespace SKEFTHawking.BHEntropyMicroscopic\n77\t\n78\topen Real\n79\t\n80\t/-! ## §1 — Kaul–Majumdar closed-form Bekenstein-Hawking entropy -/\n81\t\n82\t/--\n83\t**Kaul–Majumdar closed-form Bekenstein-Hawking entropy.**\n84\t\n85\t`S(A) = A/(4 G_N) − (3/2) log(A/(4 G_N)) + c_0`.\n86\t\n87\tThe leading `A/(4 G_N)` is fixed by the Immirzi γ tuning (NOT a\n88\tderivation; see deep-research §3). The `−(3/2)` log coefficient\n89\tIS a derivation: ½ from the Gaussian saddle + 1 from the SU(2)-singlet\n90\tprojection (`I₀ − I₁` cancellation, Kaul–Majumdar Eq. (15)).\n91\t-/\n92\tnoncomputable def kaulMajumdarS (A G_N c0 : ℝ) : ℝ :=\n93\t  A / (4 * G_N) - (3 / 2) * Real.log (A / (4 * G_N)) + c0\n94\t\n95\t/-- Reduced area `A/(4 G_N)`, used throughout the saddle-point analysis. -/\n96\tnoncomputable def reducedArea (A G_N : ℝ) : ℝ := A / (4 * G_N)\n97\t\n98\t/--\n99\t**Structural extraction of the Kaul–Majumdar log coefficient.**\n100\t\n101\t`kaulMajumdarS - leading - constant = (-3/2) · log(reducedArea)`.\n102\t\n103\tThis is the substantive \"log coefficient is exactly −3/2\" statement:\n104\tisolating the log-correction term as `S − [linear part] − [constant]`\n105\tyields exactly `−3/2 · log` of the reduced area, with no other\n106\tA-dependent contributions. Falsifies the toy possibility that c_log\n107\tcould differ from −3/2 within the Kaul-Majumdar derivation tree.\n108\t-/\n109\ttheorem kaul_majumdar_log_coefficient (A G_N c0 : ℝ) :\n110\t    kaulMajumdarS A G_N c0 - reducedArea A G_N - c0\n111\t      = (-3 / 2) * Real.log (reducedArea A G_N) := by\n112\t  unfold kaulMajumdarS reducedArea\n113\t  ring\n114\t\n115\t/--\n116\t**Kaul–Majumdar log-coefficient decomposition.**\n117\t\n118\t`c_log = c_Gaussian + c_singlet = −1/2 + (−1) = −3/2`.\n119\t\n120\tThe −1/2 comes from the standard Laplace-method asymptotic\n121\t`I₀ ~ C exp(F(0))/√(−F''(0))` (Watson's lemma); the −1 comes from\n122\tthe `I₀ − I₁` cancellation in Kaul–Majumdar Eq. (12)–(15) that\n123\tproduces an extra inverse-Hessian factor `1/(−F''(0))`.\n124\t-/\n125\ttheorem kaul_majumdar_log_decomposition :\n126\t    (-(1 : ℝ) / 2) + (-1 : ℝ) = -3 / 2 := by ring\n127\t\n128\t/--\n129\t**Sen 2013 disagreement witness (non-universality).** Heat-kernel for\n130\t4D Schwarzschild pure gravity gives `c_log = (212/45 − 3) ≈ +1.711`,\n131\tdisagreeing with the Kaul–Majumdar −3/2. Encoded as a numerical\n132\tinequality theorem to make the disagreement machine-checked.\n133\t-/\n134\tnoncomputable def senFourDimSchwarzschildLogCoeff : ℝ := (212 : ℝ) / 45 - 3\n135\t\n136\ttheorem sen_4d_disagrees_with_kaul_majumdar :\n137\t    senFourDimSchwarzschildLogCoeff ≠ -3 / 2 := by\n138\t  unfold senFourDimSchwarzschildLogCoeff\n139\t  -- 212/45 - 3 = 77/45 ≈ 1.711, which is positive, hence ≠ −3/2.\n140\t  have h : (212 : ℝ) / 45 - 3 = 77 / 45 := by norm_num\n141\t  rw [h]\n142\t  norm_num\n143\t\n144\t/-- Sen's c_log is positive (further witness against −3/2 universality). -/\n145\ttheorem sen_4d_log_coeff_pos : 0 < senFourDimSchwarzschildLogCoeff := by\n146\t  unfold senFourDimSchwarzschildLogCoeff\n147\t  norm_num\n148\t\n149\t/--\n150\t**Quantitative Sen-vs-Kaul-Majumdar disagreement bound.** The Sen 4D\n151\tSchwarzschild heat-kernel coefficient differs from the Kaul-Majumdar\n152\tSU(2)_k value by at least 3 (in absolute value). Strengthens\n153\t`sen_4d_disagrees_with_kaul_majumdar` from `≠` to `|·| > 3`, making\n154\tthe non-universality witness *quantitative* rather than merely\n155\tqualitative.\n156\t-/\n157\ttheorem sen_4d_quantitative_disagreement_bound :\n158\t    3 < senFourDimSchwarzschildLogCoeff - (-3 / 2) := by\n159\t  unfold senFourDimSchwarzschildLogCoeff\n160\t  -- 212/45 - 3 - (-3/2) = 212/45 - 3 + 3/2 = 212/45 - 3/2\n161\t  --                    = (424 - 135)/90 = 289/90 ≈ 3.21\n162\t  have : (212 : ℝ) / 45 - 3 - (-3 / 2) = 289 / 90 := by norm_num\n163\t  rw [this]; norm_num\n164\t\n165\t/-! ## §2 — Laplace-saddle limit of the Verlinde-counted entropy\n166\t                  (Wave 6a.7 — axiom retired) -/\n167\t\n168\t/-- **Puncture-number variable** `x(A) = A / (8 G_N log 2) = reducedArea / (2 log 2)`: the\n169\tSU(2) singlet-count argument whose leading log-dimension `2·x·log 2` equals the reduced area\n170\t`A/(4 G_N)`. -/\n171\tnoncomputable def verlindeArea (A G_N : ℝ) : ℝ := A / (8 * G_N * Real.log 2)\n172\t\n173\t/-- **Kaul–Majumdar additive constant** the faithful continuum entropy converges to:\n174\t`(3/2)·log(2 log 2) − ½·log π` — the change-of-variables constant `(3/2)·log(2 log 2)`\n175\t(from `x = reducedArea/(2 log 2)`) plus the Catalan principal-part constant `−½·log π`. -/\n176\tnoncomputable def kmConstant : ℝ :=\n177\t  (3 / 2) * Real.log (2 * Real.log 2) - (1 / 2) * Real.log Real.pi\n178\t\n179\t/--\n180\t**Faithful Verlinde-counted SU(2)_k horizon entropy (Wave 7C — substrate-audit #13 CLOSED).**\n181\t\n182\t`verlindeEntropy_SU2k A G_N := continuumLogCatalan (x(A))` — the LITERAL log of the\n183\tΓ-interpolated SU(2) singlet dimension `Γ(2x+1)/(Γ(x+1)·Γ(x+2))` evaluated at the puncture\n184\tvariable `x(A) = A/(8 G_N log 2)`.\n185\t\n186\tThis is a genuine, independent analytic object (the analytic continuation of the Catalan singlet\n187\tcount), **not** the saddle self-definition `:= kaulMajumdarS A G_N 0` that Wave 6a.7 shipped\n188\t(substrate-audit finding #13, \"defining-the-conclusion\"). The Kaul–Majumdar closed form\n189\t`kaulMajumdarS` is now a *derived corollary* — `gaussianSaddleAsymptotic` is the genuine `O(1/A)`\n190\trate, no longer the vacuous `|x − x| = 0`. The `−3/2` log coefficient is carried by\n191\t`ContinuumCatalan.continuumLogCatalan_isBigO` (kernel-pure), ultimately from the `Real.Gamma`\n192\tStirling-with-remainder `GammaStirling.logGamma_sub_stirlingPart_isBigO`. The discrete `O(1/m)`\n193\tanalogue is `LaplaceMethodAsymptotic.log_singletCount_sub_rate`.\n194\t-/\n195\tnoncomputable def verlindeEntropy_SU2k (A G_N : ℝ) : ℝ :=\n196\t  ContinuumCatalan.continuumLogCatalan (verlindeArea A G_N)\n197\t\n198\t/-- **Change of variables: the Kaul–Majumdar saddle IS the continuum principal part.** For\n199\t`A, G_N > 0`, `kaulMajumdarS A G_N kmConstant = 2·x(A)·log 2 − (3/2)·log x(A) − ½·log π`\n200\t*exactly* (`2·x·log 2 = A/(4 G_N)` cancels the `log 2`; the `−(3/2)·log(2 log 2)` from\n201\t`x = reducedArea/(2 log 2)` folds into `kmConstant`). -/\n202\ttheorem kaulMajumdarS_eq_continuum_principal (A G_N : ℝ) (hA : 0 < A) (hG : 0 < G_N) :\n203\t    kaulMajumdarS A G_N kmConstant\n204\t      = 2 * verlindeArea A G_N * Real.log 2 - (3 / 2) * Real.log (verlindeArea A G_N)\n205\t        - (1 / 2) * Real.log Real.pi := by\n206\t  have h2log2 : (0 : ℝ) < 2 * Real.log 2 := by positivity\n207\t  have hra : (0 : ℝ) < A / (4 * G_N) := by positivity\n208\t  have hva : verlindeArea A G_N = A / (4 * G_N) / (2 * Real.log 2) := by\n209\t    unfold verlindeArea; field_simp; ring\n210\t  have hlogva : Real.log (verlindeArea A G_N)\n211\t      = Real.log (A / (4 * G_N)) - Real.log (2 * Real.log 2) := by\n212\t    rw [hva, Real.log_div (ne_of_gt hra) (ne_of_gt h2log2)]\n213\t  have hlead : 2 * verlindeArea A G_N * Real.log 2 = A / (4 * G_N) := by\n214\t    unfold verlindeArea; field_simp; ring\n215\t  unfold kaulMajumdarS kmConstant\n216\t  rw [hlead, hlogva]; ring\n217\t\n218\t/--\n219\t**Gaussian-saddle asymptotic (Wave 7C — genuine `O(1/A)` rate).**\n220\t\n221\tFor each `G_N > 0`, the *faithful* continuum Verlinde entropy `verlindeEntropy_SU2k` converges to\n222\tthe Kaul–Majumdar closed form `kaulMajumdarS A G_N kmConstant` at rate `O(1/A)` as `A → ∞`.\n223\t\n224\tThis replaces the Wave-6a.7 vacuity: there `verlindeEntropy_SU2k := kaulMajumdarS A G_N 0`, so the\n225\tbound was the trivial `|x − x| = 0 ≤ C/A` (substrate-audit #13). Now `verlindeEntropy_SU2k` is the\n226\tliteral Γ-Catalan log-dimension and this is the genuine saddle-point statement, derived from\n227\t`ContinuumCatalan.continuumLogCatalan_isBigO` (kernel-pure, via the `Real.Gamma`\n228\tStirling-with-remainder). The additive constant is `kmConstant ≠ 0` — the literal Verlinde sum's\n229\tgenuine constant — not the prior `c₀ = 0`; and the rate constant depends on `G_N` (the puncture\n230\tvariable scales as `A/(8 G_N log 2)`), so the statement is per-`G_N` rather than uniform.\n231\t-/\n232\ttheorem gaussianSaddleAsymptotic (G_N : ℝ) (hG : 0 < G_N) :\n233\t    (fun A : ℝ => verlindeEntropy_SU2k A G_N - kaulMajumdarS A G_N kmConstant)\n234\t      =O[Filter.atTop] (fun A : ℝ => 1 / A) := by\n235\t  have hlog2 : (0 : ℝ) < Real.log 2 := Real.log_pos (by norm_num)\n236\t  have hc : (0 : ℝ) < 8 * G_N * Real.log 2 := by positivity\n237\t  -- x(A) → ∞\n238\t  have hva_tendsto : Filter.Tendsto (fun A : ℝ => verlindeArea A G_N) Filter.atTop Filter.atTop := by\n239\t    have hfun : (fun A : ℝ => verlindeArea A G_N) = (fun A : ℝ => (8 * G_N * Real.log 2)⁻¹ * A) := by\n240\t      funext A; unfold verlindeArea; rw [div_eq_inv_mul]\n241\t    rw [hfun]\n242\t    exact Filter.tendsto_id.const_mul_atTop (inv_pos.mpr hc)\n243\t  -- 1/x(A) = O(1/A) (it is a positive constant multiple of 1/A)\n244\t  have hva_bigO : (fun A : ℝ => 1 / verlindeArea A G_N) =O[Filter.atTop] (fun A : ℝ => 1 / A) := by\n245\t    have hfun : (fun A : ℝ => 1 / verlindeArea A G_N)\n246\t        = (fun A : ℝ => (8 * G_N * Real.log 2) * (1 / A)) := by\n247\t      funext A; unfold verlindeArea; rw [one_div_div]; ring\n248\t    rw [hfun]\n249\t    exact (Asymptotics.isBigO_refl (fun A : ℝ => 1 / A) Filter.atTop).const_mul_left _\n250\t  -- compose the continuum asymptotic with x(A), then match the target pointwise\n251\t  have hcomp := (ContinuumCatalan.continuumLogCatalan_isBigO.comp_tendsto hva_tendsto).trans hva_bigO\n252\t  refine hcomp.congr' ?_ (Filter.EventuallyEq.refl _ _)\n253\t  filter_upwards [Filter.eventually_gt_atTop 0] with A hA\n254\t  simp only [Function.comp_apply]\n255\t  unfold verlindeEntropy_SU2k\n256\t  rw [kaulMajumdarS_eq_continuum_principal A G_N hA hG]\n257\t\n258\t/-- **Public face of the saddle-point bound** (re-export of `gaussianSaddleAsymptotic`). -/\n259\ttheorem kaulMajumdar_asymptotic_within_OoneOverA (G_N : ℝ) (hG : 0 < G_N) :\n260\t    (fun A : ℝ => verlindeEntropy_SU2k A G_N - kaulMajumdarS A G_N kmConstant)\n261\t      =O[Filter.atTop] (fun A : ℝ => 1 / A) :=\n262\t  gaussianSaddleAsymptotic G_N hG\n263\t\n264\t/--\n265\t**Verlinde → Kaul–Majumdar large-area convergence.** The faithful continuum entropy converges to\n266\tthe Kaul–Majumdar closed form (with the genuine constant `kmConstant`) as `A → ∞`. Derived from\n267\tthe `O(1/A)` rate `gaussianSaddleAsymptotic` and `1/A → 0`.\n268\t-/\n269\ttheorem verlinde_matches_kaul_majumdar_at_large_area (G_N : ℝ) (hG : 0 < G_N) :\n270\t    Filter.Tendsto (fun A : ℝ => verlindeEntropy_SU2k A G_N - kaulMajumdarS A G_N kmConstant)\n271\t      Filter.atTop (nhds 0) := by\n272\t  have h0 : Filter.Tendsto (fun A : ℝ => 1 / A) Filter.atTop (nhds 0) := by\n273\t    simpa only [one_div] using tendsto_inv_atTop_zero\n274\t  exact (gaussianSaddleAsymptotic G_N hG).trans_tendsto h0\n275\t\n276\t/--\n277\t**Literal Verlinde-sum derivation at the `O(1/A)` rate (Wave 7C — DISCHARGED, audit-#13 closed).**\n278\t\n279\tThe faithful continuum Verlinde entropy minus its Kaul–Majumdar saddle is `O(1/A)` for every\n280\t`G_N > 0`. This is the strictly-stronger `≤ C/A` *rate* that Wave 7B left as future work (Wave 7B\n281\thad only the discrete `O(1)`; Wave 7C now has the discrete `O(1/m)` rate\n282\t`LaplaceMethodAsymptotic.log_singletCount_sub_rate` AND this continuum `O(1/A)` form). Discharged\n283\tby `gaussianSaddleAsymptotic`, ultimately from the `Real.Gamma` Stirling-with-remainder\n284\t(`GammaStirling.logGamma_sub_stirlingPart_isBigO`) + the continuum Catalan asymptotic\n285\t(`ContinuumCatalan.continuumLogCatalan_isBigO`), all kernel-pure. The earlier `≤ C/A`-against-`c₀=0`\n286\tself-definition vacuity (`|x − x| = 0`) is now fully eliminated: the entropy is the literal\n287\tΓ-Catalan log-dimension and the saddle is its genuine asymptotic limit.\n288\t-/\n289\tdef H_VerlindeKMLiteralSumDerivation : Prop :=\n290\t  ∀ G_N : ℝ, 0 < G_N →\n291\t    (fun A : ℝ => verlindeEntropy_SU2k A G_N - kaulMajumdarS A G_N kmConstant)\n292\t      =O[Filter.atTop] (fun A : ℝ => 1 / A)\n293\t\n294\t/-- **Discharge of `H_VerlindeKMLiteralSumDerivation`** (Wave 7C, kernel-pure): the faithful\n295\tcontinuum entropy meets the strong `O(1/A)` rate against its genuine Kaul–Majumdar saddle. -/\n296\ttheorem H_VerlindeKMLiteralSumDerivation_discharged : H_VerlindeKMLiteralSumDerivation :=\n297\t  fun G_N hG => gaussianSaddleAsymptotic G_N hG\n298\t\n299\t/-! ## §3 — Per-MTC abstract data carrier -/\n300\t\n301\t/--\n302\t**Abstract horizon-MTC data.** A finite label set indexing simple\n303\tobjects, per-object positive quantum dimensions, a unit object with\n304\t`d = 1`, an attainable maximum `d_max`, per-object area contributions,\n305\ta dominant simple object, and the Immirzi tuning parameter γ.\n306\t\n307\tThe MTC-categorical structure (S, T modular matrices; F, R braided\n308\tdata) is NOT formalized at this abstract level. Concrete instances\n309\tlive in `SU2kFusion`, `FibonacciMTC`, `IsingBraiding`, `S3CenterAnyons`.\n310\t-/\n311\tstructure HorizonMTCBC where\n312\t  num_objects : ℕ\n313\t  num_pos : 0 < num_objects\n314\t  quantum_dim : Fin num_objects → ℝ\n315\t  quantum_dim_pos : ∀ a, 0 < quantum_dim a\n316\t  unit_obj : Fin num_objects\n317\t  quantum_dim_unit : quantum_dim unit_obj = 1\n318\t  d_max : ℝ\n319\t  d_max_attained : ∃ a, quantum_dim a = d_max\n320\t  d_max_upper : ∀ a, quantum_dim a ≤ d_max\n321\t  dominant_obj : Fin num_objects\n322\t  γ_immirzi : ℝ\n323\t  γ_pos : 0 < γ_immirzi\n324\t\n325\tnamespace HorizonMTCBC\n326\t\n327\t/-- The unit object's quantum dimension is bounded above by `d_max`. -/\n328\ttheorem one_le_d_max (H : HorizonMTCBC) : 1 ≤ H.d_max := by\n329\t  have := H.d_max_upper H.unit_obj\n330\t  rw [H.quantum_dim_unit] at this\n331\t  exact this\n332\t\n333\t/-- `d_max > 0`: positive quantum dimensions. -/\n334\ttheorem d_max_pos (H : HorizonMTCBC) : 0 < H.d_max :=\n335\t  lt_of_lt_of_le zero_lt_one H.one_le_d_max\n336\t\n337\t/-- `log d_max ≥ 0` (since `d_max ≥ 1`). The structural F2 anchor. -/\n338\ttheorem log_d_max_nonneg (H : HorizonMTCBC) : 0 ≤ Real.log H.d_max :=\n339\t  Real.log_nonneg H.one_le_d_max\n340\t\n341\t/-- Total quantum dimension squared `D² = Σ_a d_a²`. -/\n342\tnoncomputable def globalDimSq (H : HorizonMTCBC) : ℝ :=\n343\t  ∑ a : Fin H.num_objects, (H.quantum_dim a) ^ 2\n344\t\n345\t/-- `D² > 0`: contains at least the unit's `1² = 1`. -/\n346\ttheorem globalDimSq_pos (H : HorizonMTCBC) : 0 < H.globalDimSq := by\n347\t  unfold globalDimSq\n348\t  apply Finset.sum_pos' (fun a _ => sq_nonneg _)\n349\t  exact ⟨H.unit_obj, Finset.mem_univ _, by\n350\t    rw [H.quantum_dim_unit]; norm_num⟩\n351\t\n352\t/--\n353\t**Area-law leading coefficient ansatz** (Kitaev cond-mat/0506438):\n354\t`κ_C = c · log d_max` for some O(1) prefactor `c`.\n355\t\n356\tWave 3 uses `c = 1` as a normalization choice; the physical content is\n357\tthat κ_C vanishes precisely when log d_max = 0 (abelian MTC). Falsifier\n358\tF2 of `H_HorizonBoundaryCondition` triggers when κ_C ≤ 0.\n359\t-/\n360\tnoncomputable def areaLawKappa (H : HorizonMTCBC) : ℝ := Real.log H.d_max\n361\t\n362\t/-- κ_C ≥ 0 always. -/\n363\ttheorem areaLawKappa_nonneg (H : HorizonMTCBC) : 0 ≤ H.areaLawKappa :=\n364\t  H.log_d_max_nonneg\n365\t\n366\tend HorizonMTCBC\n367\t\n368\t/-! ## §3.7 — Real modular & anomaly conditions for the horizon BC\n369\t    (Wave 8 — discharge of the `modularInvariant` / `anomalyMatch` placeholders)\n370\t\n371\tThe Wave-3 bundle `H_HorizonBoundaryCondition` (§4) carried two fields as literal\n372\t`True` placeholders: `modularInvariant` (intended: the MTC modular-data condition)\n373\tand `anomalyMatch` (intended: Walker–Wang Z₂ anomaly inflow). This section ships\n374\tthe genuine, falsifiable predicates they are wired to. -/\n375\t\n376\t/--\n377\t**Horizon modular + anomaly data.** Companion carrier to `HorizonMTCBC`, holding\n378\tthe S-matrix-bearing modular data (`PreModularData`) and the chiral central charge\n379\t`c₋`. Kept *separate* from `HorizonMTCBC` (which has external consumers —\n380\t`QECHolographyBridge`, `HolographicCFunctionMTC`) so enriching the boundary\n381\tcondition with modular structure does not ripple into those modules' carrier.\n382\t-/\n383\tstructure HorizonModularData where\n384\t  md : SKEFTHawking.PreModularData ℝ\n385\t  c_minus : ℝ\n386\t\n387\t/--\n388\t**Mod-8 perturbative-gravitational-anomaly predicate (Walker–Wang Z₂ inflow).**\n389\tThe chiral central charge has a vanishing perturbative gravitational anomaly mod 8,\n390\t`8 ∣ c₋` — exactly the mod-8 factor of the `24 = 8 × 3` framing-anomaly\n391\tdecomposition in `ModularInvarianceConstraint` (`twenty_four_decomposition`).\n392\t\n393\t**Honesty note (what this is and is NOT).** This is the *trivial-anomaly-mod-8*\n394\tcondition; it is NOT a biconditional for \"bounds a Z₂-symmetric Walker–Wang bulk\".\n395\tThe canonical Z₂ Walker–Wang example — the 3-fermion (3F) model — bounds such a\n396\tbulk yet realizes the *nontrivial* `c₋ ≡ 4 (mod 8)` class, so `8 ∣ c₋` is strictly\n397\tthe vanishing-anomaly condition, not WW-bulk-bounding. The ADW substrate's\n398\t`c₋ = 8 N_f` (`WangBridge`) satisfies `8 ∣ c₋` by construction; a chiral MTC\n399\t(`c₋ ∉ 8ℤ`, e.g. Fibonacci `14/5`, Ising `1/2`) does not.\n400\t-/\n401\tdef chiralAnomalyVanishesMod8 (c_minus : ℝ) : Prop := ∃ k : ℤ, c_minus = 8 * (k : ℝ)\n402\t\n403\tnamespace HorizonModularData\n404\t\n405\t/-- **Real modular-invariance condition** (replaces the Wave-3 `True`): the MTC's\n406\tmodular `S`-matrix is non-degenerate (`det S ≠ 0`), the data-level modularity from\n407\twhich the `(ST)³ = S²` modular-group action follows for a genuine MTC. -/\n408\tdef modularInvariant (M : HorizonModularData) : Prop := M.md.modular\n409\t\n410\t/-- **Real anomaly-inflow condition** (replaces the Wave-3 `True`): the boundary\n411\tchiral `c₋` matches the bulk Z₂ Walker–Wang inflow, i.e. `8 ∣ c₋`. -/\n412\tdef anomalyMatch (M : HorizonModularData) : Prop := chiralAnomalyVanishesMod8 M.c_minus\n413\t\n414\tend HorizonModularData\n415\t\n416\t/-- **`modularInvariant` witness.** The Fibonacci modular data is non-degenerate\n417\t(`FibonacciMTC.fib_modular`), so a Fibonacci-carrying horizon datum satisfies the\n418\treal modular-invariance condition — non-vacuously (a premodular *non*-modular\n419\tcategory with degenerate `S` fails it). -/\n420\ttheorem fibonacci_satisfies_modularInvariant :\n421\t    (HorizonModularData.mk FibonacciMTC.fibData (14 / 5)).modularInvariant :=\n422\t  FibonacciMTC.fib_modular\n423\t\n424\t/-- A degenerate-`S` premodular datum (`S = !![1,1;1,1]`, so `det S = 0`). -/\n425\tnoncomputable def degenerateSData : SKEFTHawking.PreModularData ℝ where\n426\t  n := 2\n427\t  hn := by norm_num\n428\t  S := !![1, 1; 1, 1]\n429\t  d := ![1, 1]\n430\t  N := fun _ _ _ => 0\n431\t\n432\t/-- **`modularInvariant` falsifier.** A premodular datum with a degenerate `S`-matrix\n433\t(`det S = 0`) fails `modularInvariant` — the symmetric counterpart to the two\n434\t`anomalyMatch` falsifiers, so the Wave-8 modular condition is non-vacuous in both\n435\tdirections (a real witness `fibonacci_satisfies_modularInvariant` AND a real\n436\tfalsifier). -/\n437\ttheorem degenerate_S_violates_modularInvariant :\n438\t    ¬ (HorizonModularData.mk degenerateSData 0).modularInvariant := by\n439\t  have hdet : degenerateSData.S.det = 0 := by\n440\t    unfold degenerateSData; simp [Matrix.det_fin_two]\n441\t  simpa [HorizonModularData.modularInvariant, SKEFTHawking.PreModularData.modular,\n442\t    not_ne_iff] using hdet\n443\t\n444\t/-- **`anomalyMatch` witness (ADW substrate).** The ADW chiral central charge\n445\t`c₋ = 8 N_f` (`WangBridge`) satisfies the Walker–Wang Z₂ mod-8 inflow condition for\n446\tevery generation count `N_f`. -/\n447\ttheorem adw_chiral_charge_vanishes_mod8 (N_f : ℤ) :\n448\t    chiralAnomalyVanishesMod8 (8 * (N_f : ℝ)) :=\n449\t  ⟨N_f, rfl⟩\n450\t\n451\t/-- **`anomalyMatch` falsifier (Fibonacci is chiral).** `c₋(Fib) = 14/5 ∉ 8ℤ`: a\n452\tsingle chiral MTC cannot bound a Z₂-symmetric Walker–Wang bulk. -/\n453\ttheorem fibonacci_chiral_violates_mod8 : ¬ chiralAnomalyVanishesMod8 (14 / 5) := by\n454\t  rintro ⟨k, hk⟩\n455\t  have hk' : (40 * k : ℤ) = 14 := by\n456\t    have : ((40 * k : ℤ) : ℝ) = 14 := by push_cast; linarith\n457\t    exact_mod_cast this\n458\t  omega\n459\t\n460\t/-- **`anomalyMatch` falsifier (Ising is chiral).** `c₋(Ising) = 1/2 ∉ 8ℤ`. -/\n461\ttheorem ising_chiral_violates_mod8 : ¬ chiralAnomalyVanishesMod8 (1 / 2) := by\n462\t  rintro ⟨k, hk⟩\n463\t  have hk' : (16 * k : ℤ) = 1 := by\n464\t    have : ((16 * k : ℤ) : ℝ) = 1 := by push_cast; linarith\n465\t    exact_mod_cast this\n466\t  omega\n467\t\n468\t/-- **Cross-module bridge (anomaly-match ⟹ generation constraint).** If the horizon\n469\tchiral charge is the ADW value `c₋ = 8 N_f` (so `anomalyMatch` holds mod 8) and the\n470\tpartition function is additionally fully modular-invariant (`24 ∣ c₋`), then\n471\t`3 ∣ N_f` — recovering `ModularInvarianceConstraint.modular_generation_constraint`\n472\tfrom the horizon boundary condition. -/\n473\ttheorem horizon_anomalyMatch_modular_forces_three_generations\n474\t    (N_f : ℕ) (hN : 0 < N_f) (h24 : (24 : ℤ) ∣ 8 * (N_f : ℤ)) : 3 ∣ N_f :=\n475\t  SKEFTHawking.modular_generation_constraint N_f hN h24\n476\t\n477\t/-! ## §4 — Tracked-hypothesis bundle `H_HorizonBoundaryCondition` -/\n478\t\n479\t/--\n480\t**Tracked hypothesis: the horizon-bounding MTC carries the BH entropy.**\n481\t\n482\tBundles the five conditions a candidate MTC at the horizon must satisfy\n483\tfor `S(A) = A/(4 G_N^emerg) + log corrections` to make sense:\n484\t\n485\t  - `positivity`     — entropy ≥ 0 for all non-negative A\n486\t  - `areaLeading`    — leading scaling is κ·A with κ > 0\n487\t  - `secondLaw`      — entropy is monotone non-decreasing in A\n488\t  - `modularInvariant` — the MTC modular `S`-matrix is non-degenerate\n489\t                          (`M.modularInvariant := M.md.modular`; the data-level\n490\t                          modularity from which `(ST)³ = S²` follows). **Wave 8:\n491\t                          real Prop, no longer a `True` placeholder (§3.7).**\n492\t  - `anomalyMatch`   — boundary chiral `c₋` matches the bulk Z₂ Walker–Wang\n493\t                          inflow, `8 ∣ c₋` (`M.anomalyMatch`). **Wave 8: real\n494\t                          Prop, no longer a `True` placeholder (§3.7).**\n495\t\n496\tThe bundle now carries the companion modular datum `M : HorizonModularData`\n497\t(S-matrix + `c₋`), kept separate from `HorizonMTCBC` to avoid rippling into the\n498\tcarrier's external consumers. It is genuinely non-trivial: every conjunct admits a\n499\tfalsifier (§5, §6.7) AND the whole bundle is satisfiable\n500\t(`fibonacci_horizon_satisfies_H_HorizonBoundaryCondition`, §6.7). The two Wave-8\n501\tfields are independently witnessed (`fibonacci_satisfies_modularInvariant`,\n502\t`adw_chiral_charge_vanishes_mod8`) and falsified (`fibonacci_chiral_violates_mod8`,\n503\t`ising_chiral_violates_mod8`).\n504\t\n505\t**Novelty flag.** No published paper pins the MTC for an ADW substrate.\n506\tThis Prop is the formal record of the Wave 3 tracked hypothesis (Wave-8 hardened).\n507\t-/\n508\tstructure H_HorizonBoundaryCondition (H : HorizonMTCBC)\n509\t    (M : HorizonModularData)\n510\t    (S_horizon : HorizonMTCBC → ℝ → ℝ) : Prop where\n511\t  positivity      : ∀ A, 0 ≤ A → 0 ≤ S_horizon H A\n512\t  areaLeading     : 0 < H.areaLawKappa\n513\t  secondLaw       : Monotone (S_horizon H)\n514\t  modularInvariant : M.modularInvariant  -- real: S-matrix non-degenerate (§3.7)\n515\t  anomalyMatch    : M.anomalyMatch        -- real: 8 ∣ c₋ Walker–Wang inflow (§3.7)\n516\t\n517\t/-! ## §5 — Five falsifier theorems for `H_HorizonBoundaryCondition` -/\n518\t\n519\t/--\n520\t**F1 (positivity falsifier).** Any candidate `S_horizon` violating\n521\t`S ≥ 0` at any non-negative A is rejected.\n522\t-/\n523\ttheorem H_HorizonBoundaryCondition_falsifier_positivity\n524\t    (H : HorizonMTCBC) (M : HorizonModularData) (S_horizon : HorizonMTCBC → ℝ → ℝ)\n525\t    (A₀ : ℝ) (hA₀ : 0 ≤ A₀) (hneg : S_horizon H A₀ < 0) :\n526\t    ¬ H_HorizonBoundaryCondition H M S_horizon := by\n527\t  intro h\n528\t  exact absurd (h.positivity A₀ hA₀) (not_le.mpr hneg)\n529\t\n530\t/--\n531\t**F2 (area-law falsifier).** Any candidate violating `κ_C > 0` is\n532\trejected. This is the abelian-MTC falsifier: pure-`d_a = 1` MTCs\n533\t(toric code, `D(ℤ_n)`) all give `d_max = 1`, hence `log d_max = 0`,\n534\thence `κ_C = 0`, triggering F2.\n535\t-/\n536\ttheorem H_HorizonBoundaryCondition_falsifier_logBound\n537\t    (H : HorizonMTCBC) (M : HorizonModularData) (S_horizon : HorizonMTCBC → ℝ → ℝ)\n538\t    (hkap : H.areaLawKappa = 0) :\n539\t    ¬ H_HorizonBoundaryCondition H M S_horizon := by\n540\t  intro h\n541\t  exact absurd h.areaLeading (by rw [hkap]; exact lt_irrefl 0)\n542\t\n543\t/--\n544\t**F3 (second-law falsifier).** Any candidate `S_horizon` non-monotone\n545\tin A is rejected.\n546\t-/\n547\ttheorem H_HorizonBoundaryCondition_falsifier_secondLaw\n548\t    (H : HorizonMTCBC) (M : HorizonModularData) (S_horizon : HorizonMTCBC → ℝ → ℝ)\n549\t    (A₁ A₂ : ℝ) (hA : A₁ ≤ A₂) (hviol : S_horizon H A₂ < S_horizon H A₁) :\n550\t    ¬ H_HorizonBoundaryCondition H M S_horizon := by\n551\t  intro h\n552\t  exact absurd (h.secondLaw hA) (not_le.mpr hviol)\n553\t\n554\t-- F4 (the quantitative 1/4-coefficient falsifier\n555\t-- `H_HorizonBoundaryCondition_falsifier_quarterCoefficient`) is relocated to §6.7\n556\t-- below — its substantive form depends on `kaulMajumdar_S_at_4GN` (defined in §6).\n557\t\n558\t/--\n559\t**F5 (substantive structural corollary of the bundle).**\n560\tThe bundle's five conjuncts (positivity, areaLeading, secondLaw,\n561\tmodularInvariant, anomalyMatch) jointly imply two derived facts that\n562\tneither field alone discharges:\n563\t\n564\t  (i) **non-abelian-MTC requirement** — there exists a simple object\n565\t      with `quantum_dim > 1`. This is what blocks toric code,\n566\t      `D(ℤ_n)`, and any other purely abelian MTC from carrying the\n567\t      Wave 3 horizon BC.\n568\t  (ii) **monotone non-negative envelope** — for any `0 ≤ A₁ ≤ A₂`,\n569\t      the entropy candidate is non-negative at `A₁` and bounded above\n570\t      by its value at `A₂`. This sandwiches `S_horizon H A` between\n571\t      `0` and any later area sample.\n572\t\n573\tThe first conclusion combines `areaLeading` with `d_max_attained` and\n574\tthe strict-monotonicity of `Real.log` to upgrade `0 < log d_max` to\n575\t`∃ a, 1 < d_a` — a derived non-projection statement. The second\n576\tcombines `positivity` with `secondLaw` to produce the entropy sandwich.\n577\t\n578\tThis theorem is the post-strengthening (2026-04-26 followup-pass)\n579\treplacement for the trivial-projection theorem\n580\t`H_HorizonBoundaryCondition_implies_areaLawKappa_pos` that an\n581\tadversarial review correctly flagged as a single-field projection\n582\t(`h.areaLeading`) masquerading as an F5 falsifier. The single-field\n583\tprojection has been removed — callers needing only `0 < H.areaLawKappa`\n584\tcan use `h.areaLeading` directly (which IS the field projection,\n585\thonestly named).\n586\t-/\n587\ttheorem H_HorizonBoundaryCondition_implies_nonabelian_envelope\n588\t    (H : HorizonMTCBC) (M : HorizonModularData) (S_horizon : HorizonMTCBC → ℝ → ℝ)\n589\t    (h : H_HorizonBoundaryCondition H M S_horizon)\n590\t    {A₁ A₂ : ℝ} (hA₁ : 0 ≤ A₁) (hA : A₁ ≤ A₂) :\n591\t    (∃ a : Fin H.num_objects, 1 < H.quantum_dim a) ∧\n592\t    0 ≤ S_horizon H A₁ ∧ S_horizon H A₁ ≤ S_horizon H A₂ := by\n593\t  refine ⟨?_, h.positivity A₁ hA₁, h.secondLaw hA⟩\n594\t  -- areaLeading gives 0 < Real.log H.d_max ⇒ 1 < H.d_max ⇒ some d_a > 1.\n595\t  have h_log_pos : 0 < Real.log H.d_max := h.areaLeading\n596\t  have h_dmax_gt_one : 1 < H.d_max :=\n597\t    (Real.log_pos_iff H.d_max_pos.le).mp h_log_pos\n598\t  obtain ⟨a, ha⟩ := H.d_max_attained\n599\t  exact ⟨a, ha ▸ h_dmax_gt_one⟩\n600\t\n601\t/--\n602\t**F2 falsifier — concrete abelian-MTC form.** If every simple object\n603\tof `H` has `quantum_dim = 1` (abelian MTC: toric code, `D(ℤ_n)`, etc.),\n604\tthen `d_max = 1`, hence `log d_max = 0`, hence `areaLawKappa = 0`,\n605\thence no `S_horizon` candidate can satisfy `H_HorizonBoundaryCondition`.\n606\t\n607\tThis is the substantive Wave 3 falsifier: \\emph{abelian MTCs are ruled\n608\tout as horizon BCs by the area-law leading-scaling condition F2}. This\n609\tis the deep-research-§4 verdict made machine-checked.\n610\t-/\n611\ttheorem abelian_MTC_falsifies_H_HorizonBoundaryCondition\n612\t    (H : HorizonMTCBC) (M : HorizonModularData) (S_horizon : HorizonMTCBC → ℝ → ℝ)\n613\t    (h_abelian : ∀ a, H.quantum_dim a = 1) :\n614\t    ¬ H_HorizonBoundaryCondition H M S_horizon := by\n615\t  -- d_max ≤ 1 from h_abelian + d_max_upper; combined with one_le_d_max gives d_max = 1.\n616\t  have h_dmax_eq_one : H.d_max = 1 := by\n617\t    obtain ⟨a, ha⟩ := H.d_max_attained\n618\t    rw [← ha, h_abelian a]\n619\t  have h_kappa_zero : H.areaLawKappa = 0 := by\n620\t    unfold HorizonMTCBC.areaLawKappa\n621\t    rw [h_dmax_eq_one, Real.log_one]\n622\t  exact H_HorizonBoundaryCondition_falsifier_logBound H M S_horizon h_kappa_zero\n623\t\n624\t/-! ## §6 — SU(2)_k Kaul-Majumdar specialization (Outcome-2 sub-corollary) -/\n625\t\n626\t/--\n627\t**Concrete SU(2)_k Kaul-Majumdar instantiation.** A `HorizonMTCBC`\n628\twith `num_objects = k+1` and quantum dimensions `d_j = sin((2j+1)π/(k+2))/sin(π/(k+2))`\n629\tindexed by `j = 0, ..., k`. Wave 3 ships an *abstract* SU(2)_k constructor;\n630\tthe concrete formalization of d_j lives in the existing `SU2kFusion` module.\n631\t\n632\tHere we record the entropy candidate and prove the structural log\n633\tcoefficient (its saddle-point limit is `gaussianSaddleAsymptotic`, now a theorem).\n634\t-/\n635\tnoncomputable def kaulMajumdar_S_KM (G_N : ℝ) : ℝ → ℝ :=\n636\t  fun A => kaulMajumdarS A G_N 0\n637\t\n638\t/-- Kaul-Majumdar entropy at A = 4 G_N is exactly 0 (the leading - log = 1 - (3/2)·0). -/\n639\ttheorem kaulMajumdar_S_at_4GN (G_N : ℝ) (hG : 0 < G_N) :\n640\t    kaulMajumdarS (4 * G_N) G_N 0 = 1 := by\n641\t  unfold kaulMajumdarS\n642\t  have h4 : (4 : ℝ) * G_N / (4 * G_N) = 1 := by\n643\t    field_simp\n644\t  rw [h4]\n645\t  rw [Real.log_one]\n646\t  ring\n647\t\n648\t/-- Kaul-Majumdar entropy is positive for `A` sufficiently large. -/\n649\ttheorem kaulMajumdar_S_pos_at_e_squared (G_N : ℝ) (hG : 0 < G_N) :\n650\t    0 < kaulMajumdarS (4 * G_N * Real.exp 2) G_N 0 := by\n651\t  unfold kaulMajumdarS\n652\t  -- Reduced area = exp(2). log(exp 2) = 2. So S = exp(2) - (3/2)·2 + 0 = exp(2) - 3.\n653\t  have hpos : (0 : ℝ) < 4 * G_N := by positivity\n654\t  have h_red : 4 * G_N * Real.exp 2 / (4 * G_N) = Real.exp 2 := by\n655\t    field_simp\n656\t  rw [h_red, Real.log_exp]\n657\t  -- Goal: 0 < Real.exp 2 - 3 / 2 * 2 + 0\n658\t  have h_e2_gt : (3 : ℝ) < Real.exp 2 := by\n659\t    have h := Real.exp_one_gt_d9   -- e > 2.71828...\n660\t    -- exp(2) = (exp 1)^2 > 2.71^2 ≈ 7.34\n661\t    have h_pow : (2.71828 : ℝ)^2 < (Real.exp 1)^2 := by\n662\t      apply sq_lt_sq' <;> linarith [Real.exp_one_gt_d9]\n663\t    have h_exp_two : Real.exp 2 = (Real.exp 1)^2 := by\n664\t      rw [show (2 : ℝ) = 1 + 1 from by norm_num, Real.exp_add]\n665\t      ring\n666\t    rw [h_exp_two]\n667\t    nlinarith [h_pow]\n668\t  linarith\n669\t\n670\t/-! ## §6.5 — Non-vacuous-instance witness (Fibonacci-shape) -/\n671\t\n672\t/--\n673\t**Fibonacci-shape `HorizonMTCBC` instance.** A `HorizonMTCBC` carrying\n674\ttwo simple objects (vacuum + dominant), with quantum dimensions\n675\t`d_0 = 1`, `d_1 = (1 + √5)/2 = φ`, `d_max = φ`, Immirzi γ = γ_M.\n676\t\n677\tThe real-Fibonacci F-symbols and modular-S data are formalized in\n678\t`FibonacciMTC.lean` (proven, zero sorry, decide over `ℚ(√5)`);\n679\tthis Lean structure is the BC-data carrier shape used by Wave 3\n680\twithout re-formalizing the categorical content.\n681\t-/\n682\tnoncomputable def fibonacciHorizonBC : HorizonMTCBC where\n683\t  num_objects := 2\n684\t  num_pos := by decide\n685\t  quantum_dim := fun a => if a.val = 0 then 1 else (1 + Real.sqrt 5) / 2\n686\t  quantum_dim_pos := by\n687\t    intro a\n688\t    by_cases h : a.val = 0\n689\t    · simp [h]\n690\t    · simp [h]\n691\t      have h5 : (0 : ℝ) ≤ 5 := by norm_num\n692\t      have hsqrt : (0 : ℝ) ≤ Real.sqrt 5 := {"parentUuid":"1d74bfb5-bdc4-4547-98a6-fa6c41ae0b36","isSidechain":true,"promptId":"d7b89794-41f0-46fe-9a20-6d198f8f624f","agentId":"a78a58dec52c8d1d6","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01NEQABaKKrnXQ73TwQbcqDb","type":"tool_result","content":"1\timport SKEFTHawking.Basic\n2\timport SKEFTHawking.HeatKernelExpansion\n3\timport SKEFTHawking.MicroscopicCoefficientMatch\n4\timport SKEFTHawking.BHEntropyMicroscopic\n5\timport Mathlib\n6\t\n7\t/-!\n8\t# Frolov–Fursaev induced-gravity 1/4 — Phase 6a Wave 9 (center-bridge C)\n9\t\n10\tCloses **Gate A.2**: derive the Bekenstein–Hawking leading coefficient `1/(4 G_N)` in the\n11\tADW Sakharov induced-gravity substrate WITHOUT γ-tuning. The conditional\n12\t`frolov_fursaev_quarter_coefficient` is, per the deep-research verdict\n13\t(`Lit-Search/Phase-6a/6a-Immirzi-area-gap-independence-for-Wave8.md`):\n14\t\n15\t  `H_Sakharov (G_N fully induced) ∧ (S_BH = S_ent) ∧ (S_ent = Frolov–Fursaev a₂ form) ⟹ S_BH = A/(4 G_N)`.\n16\t\n17\t**Anti-vacuity (strengthening checklist #5).** NONE of the three antecedents is `S = A/4G`:\n18\t(i) the Sakharov induction condition `G_N = G_N_from_a2 = 12π/(N_f Λ²)` (no bare action;\n19\t`HeatKernelExpansion`); (ii) the entanglement identification `S_BH = S_ent` (Sorkin–Bombelli);\n20\t(iii) the Frolov–Fursaev–Zelnikov / Susskind–Uglum heat-kernel result\n21\t`S_ent = (N_f Λ²/(48π))·A`. The `1/4` is the ratio `48 : 12 = 4 : 1` — the SAME Seeley–DeWitt\n22\t`a₂` coefficient fixes both the induced `G_N` (EH, `12π`) and the horizon entanglement entropy\n23\t(`48π`), and their ratio is exactly 4. So the `1/4` emerges algebraically, not by tuning γ\n24\t(Bianchi arXiv:1204.5122 corroborates γ-independence; the LQG counting `−3/2` is Wave 7B).\n25\t\n26\t**Modeling note (checklist #5, honest input).** The conical-deficit replica derivation of the\n27\t`48π` prefactor is not formalized (Mathlib lacks conical heat kernels); it enters as a NAMED,\n28\tCITABLE, FALSIFIABLE physical input — a hypothesis, NOT an axiom. `frolov_fursaev_falsifier_wrong_coeff`\n29\tshows the coefficient is load-bearing: any `c ≠ N_f Λ²/(48π)` breaks the `A/(4G)` match.\n30\t\n31\tRefs: Frolov–Fursaev–Zelnikov, Nucl. Phys. B 486 (1997), hep-th/9607104; Susskind–Uglum,\n32\thep-th/9401070; Jacobson, gr-qc/9404039.\n33\t-/\n34\t\n35\tnamespace SKEFTHawking\n36\tnamespace InducedGravityEntropy\n37\t\n38\topen Real\n39\t\n40\t/--\n41\t**Frolov–Fursaev horizon entanglement-entropy area density.** The leading (area-law)\n42\tentanglement entropy of `N_f` Dirac fermions across the horizon, from the Seeley–DeWitt `a₂`\n43\theat-kernel coefficient (conical-deficit replica trick): `S_ent = (N_f Λ²/(48π))·A`. The\n44\tcoefficient is the FFZ/Susskind–Uglum result — the SAME `a₂` that induces `G_N`\n45\t(`HeatKernelExpansion.G_N_from_a2 = 12π/(N_f Λ²)`), with the heat-kernel-to-EH ratio fixed to 4\n46\t(`48 = 4·12`). [The `48π` prefactor is a documented physical input, not derived here — see the\n47\tmodule header and `frolov_fursaev_falsifier_wrong_coeff`.]\n48\t-/\n49\tnoncomputable def entanglementEntropyAreaLeading (N_f Λ A : ℝ) : ℝ :=\n50\t  N_f * Λ ^ 2 / (48 * Real.pi) * A\n51\t\n52\t/-- **Sakharov induction condition.** The physical Newton constant is the fully-induced value\n53\t(no bare gravitational action): `G_N = G_N_from_a2 Λ N_f = 12π/(N_f Λ²)`. -/\n54\tdef H_Sakharov (Λ N_f G_N : ℝ) : Prop := G_N = HeatKernelExpansion.G_N_from_a2 Λ N_f\n55\t\n56\t/-- **Bridge: Sakharov induction ⟺ the substrate's `α_ADW = 1` (δG = 0).** Ties `H_Sakharov` to\n57\t`MicroscopicCoefficientMatch.matchResidual` (the existing Wave-5 δG residual): the physical\n58\tNewton constant `gNMicroscopic = α·G_N_from_a2` is the fully-induced value iff `α_ADW = 1`. -/\n59\ttheorem H_Sakharov_iff_alpha_unity {Λ N_f α_ADW : ℝ} (hΛ : 0 < Λ) (hN : 0 < N_f) :\n60\t    H_Sakharov Λ N_f (MicroscopicCoefficientMatch.gNMicroscopic Λ N_f α_ADW) ↔ α_ADW = 1 := by\n61\t  rw [← MicroscopicCoefficientMatch.matchResidual_eq_zero_iff_alpha_unity hΛ hN,\n62\t      MicroscopicCoefficientMatch.matchResidual, H_Sakharov, sub_eq_zero]\n63\t\n64\t/-- **The 1/4 ratio (substantive content).** The Frolov–Fursaev entanglement area density equals\n65\t`A/(4 · G_N^induced)` — i.e. the heat-kernel `a₂` ratio is `48 : 12 = 4 : 1`. This is the\n66\talgebraic heart: the `1/4` is forced by the shared `a₂`, with no free parameter. -/\n67\ttheorem entanglement_area_eq_quarter_inv_G_induced (A Λ N_f : ℝ) (hΛ : 0 < Λ) (hN : 0 < N_f) :\n68\t    entanglementEntropyAreaLeading N_f Λ A\n69\t      = A / (4 * HeatKernelExpansion.G_N_from_a2 Λ N_f) := by\n70\t  unfold entanglementEntropyAreaLeading HeatKernelExpansion.G_N_from_a2\n71\t  have hπ : Real.pi ≠ 0 := Real.pi_ne_zero\n72\t  have hN' : N_f ≠ 0 := ne_of_gt hN\n73\t  have hΛ' : Λ ≠ 0 := ne_of_gt hΛ\n74\t  field_simp\n75\t  ring\n76\t\n77\t/--\n78\t**Frolov–Fursaev induced-gravity quarter coefficient (THE conditional, Gate A.2).** Given the\n79\tSakharov induction condition (`G_N` fully induced) and the entanglement identification\n80\t(`S_BH = S_ent`), with the Frolov–Fursaev heat-kernel `S_ent` coefficient, the black-hole entropy\n81\tis exactly `A/(4 G_N)` — the `1/4` from the `48:12` `a₂` ratio, NOT tuned. None of the three\n82\tantecedents contains `S = A/4G`.\n83\t-/\n84\ttheorem frolov_fursaev_quarter_coefficient\n85\t    (A Λ N_f G_N S_BH S_ent : ℝ) (hΛ : 0 < Λ) (hN : 0 < N_f)\n86\t    (h_Sakharov : H_Sakharov Λ N_f G_N)\n87\t    (h_ident : S_BH = S_ent)\n88\t    (h_heatKernel : S_ent = entanglementEntropyAreaLeading N_f Λ A) :\n89\t    S_BH = A / (4 * G_N) := by\n90\t  rw [h_ident, h_heatKernel, h_Sakharov, entanglement_area_eq_quarter_inv_G_induced A Λ N_f hΛ hN]\n91\t\n92\t/-- **Dirac witness.** For `N_f > 0` Dirac fermions at the Sakharov point, the conditional fires:\n93\twith `G_N` the induced value and `S_BH = S_ent =` the FF area density, `S_BH = A/(4 G_N)`. -/\n94\ttheorem frolov_fursaev_dirac_witness (A Λ N_f : ℝ) (hΛ : 0 < Λ) (hN : 0 < N_f) :\n95\t    entanglementEntropyAreaLeading N_f Λ A\n96\t      = A / (4 * HeatKernelExpansion.G_N_from_a2 Λ N_f) :=\n97\t  frolov_fursaev_quarter_coefficient A Λ N_f (HeatKernelExpansion.G_N_from_a2 Λ N_f)\n98\t    (entanglementEntropyAreaLeading N_f Λ A) (entanglementEntropyAreaLeading N_f Λ A)\n99\t    hΛ hN rfl rfl rfl\n100\t\n101\t/-- **Falsifier (the 48π coefficient is load-bearing).** If `S_ent = c·A` for any coefficient\n102\t`c ≠ N_f Λ²/(48π)` (a heat-kernel coefficient other than Frolov–Fursaev's), the induced-gravity\n103\tmatch `S_BH = A/(4 G_N)` FAILS. So the `1/4` genuinely depends on the FF coefficient — it is not\n104\tvacuously true for any input. -/\n105\ttheorem frolov_fursaev_falsifier_wrong_coeff\n106\t    (A Λ N_f c : ℝ) (hA : 0 < A) (hΛ : 0 < Λ) (hN : 0 < N_f)\n107\t    (hc : c ≠ N_f * Λ ^ 2 / (48 * Real.pi)) :\n108\t    c * A ≠ A / (4 * HeatKernelExpansion.G_N_from_a2 Λ N_f) := by\n109\t  rw [← entanglement_area_eq_quarter_inv_G_induced A Λ N_f hΛ hN, entanglementEntropyAreaLeading]\n110\t  intro h\n111\t  exact hc (mul_right_cancel₀ (ne_of_gt hA) h)\n112\t\n113\t/-- **Consistency with the Kaul–Majumdar leading term.** The Frolov–Fursaev induced-gravity\n114\t`A/(4 G_N)` is exactly the leading (area-law) part of the Wave-3 `kaulMajumdarS` closed form\n115\t`A/(4 G_N) − (3/2) log(A/(4 G_N))` at the induced `G_N`. The two routes agree on the `1/4`;\n116\tWave 7B supplies the `−3/2` log from the literal count. -/\n117\ttheorem frolov_fursaev_matches_kaulMajumdar_leading (A Λ N_f : ℝ) (hΛ : 0 < Λ) (hN : 0 < N_f) :\n118\t    entanglementEntropyAreaLeading N_f Λ A\n119\t      = BHEntropyMicroscopic.kaulMajumdarS A (HeatKernelExpansion.G_N_from_a2 Λ N_f) 0\n120\t        + (3 / 2) * Real.log (A / (4 * HeatKernelExpansion.G_N_from_a2 Λ N_f)) := by\n121\t  rw [entanglement_area_eq_quarter_inv_G_induced A Λ N_f hΛ hN]\n122\t  unfold BHEntropyMicroscopic.kaulMajumdarS\n123\t  ring\n124\t\n125\tend InducedGravityEntropy\n126\tend SKEFTHawking\n127\t"}]},"uuid":"67c8b8a9-89d9-4a86-ad74-7db1258e7db2","timestamp":"2026-08-15T19:38:04.314Z","sourceToolAssistantUUID":"1d74bfb5-bdc4-4547-98a6-fa6c41ae0b36","userType":"external","entrypoint":"claude-desktop","cwd":"/Users/johnroehm/Programming/PythonEnvironments/Physics/Fluid-Based-Physics-Research/SK_EFT_Hawking","sessionId":"6cf37aa2-f1c7-4e33-a712-f17c2d75d99b","version":"2.1.229","gitBranch":"HEAD","slug":"swift-singing-llama"}
